utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Djosan, you remain subject to the declaration that you made. Mr. Nice has some questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Further cross-examination by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, of course getting documents late and not having anything like the facilities to translate them in full means that we first of all guess which passages are going to be most interesting, and we've managed to get some of those translated, but I suspect I will in part inevitably be asking the witness to look at the original and to read entries from the overhead -- the text on the overhead projector. I also don't wish to take very long with this witness, if I can possibly avoid it, for many reasons. Does the Chamber have copies of the Djosan war diary in its now complete form?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Only in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In B/C/S. That's fine. The pages we selected for translation, I think, can be distributed, and it amounts to some 25 pages. I think they've got the original text attached to them, but -- the numbering is slightly curious at the bottom but don't worry about that. What you will have now is a clip of papers that is numbered apparently 1 of 25, but you'll see that the first sequence goes to page 12, I think, and then the next sequence starts off at -- 13, goes to 13, I think, and then it starts off at another series of 12 pages and then there are some pages behind it, but the English translations are at least chronological even if they are not sequential for every day. So that's what we've got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one correction. Mr. Nice said that this was Djosan's war diary. This isn't Djosan's war diary, it is the war diary of the command of the 52nd Brigade of the PVO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Milosevic's microphone be adjusted, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether you heard me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear you. That's technically correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I may also seek to refer to Delic's war diary. I don't know if the Court has access to that at all. If the Court doesn't have access to Delic's war diary, we'll just have to make that available on the overhead projector. I'll just try and activate once more on part of my system. If it doesn't work, I'll live without it. It doesn't seem to be working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Djosan, the process of recording events in war diaries and the hierarchy of command is such that, in general, what appears in your war diary should be consistent with what appears in Delic's war diary. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question, but I'd like to say something before I go ahead to answer any of the questions. I'd like to have my map placed here, the one that I brought in last time, because I think that any discussion without a map on the board would be incomplete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let us see whether you really need it. But in the meantime, it will be at hand and the court deputy will bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to -- I'm going to start with a very simple topic that you may not have been asked to deal with very much, and it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Oh, Your Honours, may I be assured that the other witness, whose evidence has been interrupted, is not -- doesn't have access to the broadcast of this material at this moment. I'm sure that is the position, but it would be important that he shouldn't have access to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll ask the court deputy to see to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's a -- there's a place called Nogavac. Did anything happen at Nogavac on the 1st or 2nd of April of which you were aware?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Specifically, I can't remember anything actually happening at that point in time, but there's another map. May I please ask that the other map be shown that shows this area in greater detail, the smaller map which relates to Djakovica specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no recollection of anything happening at Nogavac, which the Chamber can find just slightly to the east of Celine and just north of Velika Krusa on page 10 of the standard atlas, Exhibit 83. Well, tell me this, please, Mr. Djosan - you were in charge of anti-aircraft operations - did VJ planes fly at all during the bombing of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The bombing of Kosovo started with the bombing of Yugoslavia. And when the bombing in Yugoslavia started, in the first stage the VJ planes were flying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, until there was complete air control. But helicopters flew after that, when the need arose, to pull out the wounded, and there were medical corps helicopters flying as well, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until what stage do you say there was flying of this type of -- or was it throughout the bombing campaign?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. Medical corps helicopters would fly from time to time during the entire operation, that is to say the aggression against our country, but fighter planes ceased to fly in those very first days when there were no resources for them to fly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, we may hear other evidence from other Defence witnesses, or we may have heard some already, to the effect that there was no flying, no operational flying by VJ planes, and I want you to look, please, at a passage in "As Seen, As Told," which we'll show to you I hope in the B/C/S. I'm sorry I haven't given Ms. Dicklich earlier warning of this. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you show this to the -- that to the witness and can you display on the overhead projector that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, this is a passage from "As Seen, As Told," and you've got the B/C/S version of it. We can see it on the overhead projector, and it relates to Nogavac, and on the right-hand side of the screen, we see this: "Many people remained in Nogavac, staying in burnt-out houses until on or around the 1st or 2nd of April, when Nogavac was bombed by Serbian aircraft. At first it was thought that the dropped bombs had been dropped by NATO, but one interviewee stated that he'd heard on the news that they were Serbian aircraft. More than a hundred civilians were killed and many others were injured when houses they were sheltering in were hit in this attack. Some of the houses had as many as 60 to 100 people sheltering in them. The next day, VJ and police entered the village and forced the villagers to bury the dead in a mass grave which was then covered over using a bulldozer. The villagers were then robbed and forced to leave the village." Now, that's a summary of matters which is expressed in "As Seen, As Told." It features in the indictment, and it suggests that VJ planes were used to kill many Kosovo Albanians. Is that correct? Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I've given my answer with respect to that book, or my testimony with respect to the book and my opinion about what it says in that book "As Seen, As Told." First of all, I don't know who saw, and I don't know who it was who told. So I don't like having quotations from the book quoted, the origin of which I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Colonel, would you just answer the question. Did the event described by the Prosecutor take place; that is, VJ planes bombing Nogavac? Mr. Nice, what paragraph in the indictment is this? I think we just found it. I think we just found it. 63(a)(i).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that if there was a bombing, your case, your evidence may be, although you didn't remember it earlier, that if there was a bombing at Nogavac on the 1st or 2nd of April, it must have been a bombing by NATO, yes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: If there was bombing, then yes, it was NATO who did the bombing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't remember it this morning, but tell me, if there was a bombing of the kind that we've heard of, a hundred people killed, is that something you'd expect to find recorded in a war diary, either yours or Delic's?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: In my war diary that needn't have been recorded in view of the fact that in my war diary you will find events which are exclusively linked to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'm not sure whether we've identified the correct paragraph, but I don't see where there is any allegation of a VJ plane bombing Nogavac in 63(a)(i). Or is it maybe somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It may be somewhere else or it may be that -- and I was acting on the basis -- I can tell you this: In preparation for this, I was acting on the basis of questions that the accused was asking of the witness who has been interrupted as to the detail of what was done at Nogavac. I haven't yet checked it in the indictment. I believe it to be referred in the indictment, but if I'm wrong about that, then I'll withdraw that suggestion, but the evidence is still there from "As Seen, As Told," and the point that I'm exploring loses none of its validity, but I'll try and find the point in the indictment and see if there is any further reference to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Djosan, will you now please go to your diary for the 1st of April of 1999, which I'd like --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I haven't answered yet, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I haven't given you an answer. First of all, Mr. Milosevic never mentioned Nogavac at all to me. You can look through your papers. So there was nothing said by Mr. Milosevic about that, so I could not have made the entry. My memory is good, so you can, of course, check it out, but that's what I say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see -- will you now please look at your war diary, or the war diary of your unit, for the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the usher please make it -- display it on the overhead projector if Ms. Dicklich has got another copy, and if the Chamber can find it, they can find where we're looking at. It's page -- they're page numbered, I think, and it's page number 5. No. Can we put the original on the overhead projector for the witness, please, or if he's got his diary there. We don't have, I think -- yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at this passage in your diary, you'll find two things, and we do have a translation of this passage in English, but you'll see as you look through it there's absolutely no reference to Nogavac being bombed at all. Have a look through the 1st of April and the 2nd of April, just to cover both days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next page on the overhead projector, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to answer straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think that there's been a completely erroneous interpretation of the role of the 52nd Artillery Battalion of the air defence unit. In my war diary I recorded entries which relate to Djakovica, to Djakovica, exclusively to Djakovica. So this area is outside Djakovica, and that is why no entry was made. Now, my units were deployed. I had --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pause for a minute because we've got the point but I still want you to please follow with me the questions that I'm asking. Would you now look at the bottom of the page that's displayed at the moment - and the Chamber can find a translation for this on page 12 of 26, as I think it is registered - and it says this, does it not: "There were no NATO airstrikes against units of our brigade today nor any firing by our forces at NATO aircraft." And if we look at Delic's diary, although I'm not going to trouble you with it again unless -- it says in terms that there were no attacks of any consequence on that day. And what I'd like your help with, please, by reference to the diaries is how it could be, if NATO had bombed Nogavac and killed a hundred people, that the war diaries, yours or Delic's, would make no reference to it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'll tell you right away. NATO bombed Aleksinac, and there is no entry about that in either my diary or Delic's diary. What is entered into a war diary are events which are of key importance and have a key effect on a particular unit. Had a single soldier of Delic's been killed there, that would have been entered. So as I say, not all NATO action in Djakovica was even recorded in my diary if there were no soldiers killed or facilities targeted or resources destroyed, and that is why there is no mention of that in Delic's diary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you just go to the end of the month. If you'd go now, please, to the 30th of April, which we can see in the original B/C/S text at what is page 36, marked as the 38th day of the war. If you could do that for us, please, Mr. Djosan. In the original, page 36, top right-hand corner, also registered as "38 dan rata," and if we can -- I'm not sure that we have translation of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 8 of 12. Your Honour is very helpful. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we see there is that you were instructed, or your war diary records - I'll just find it again - "OCPRK was ordered not to shoot at targets -" this is at 0600 hours - "because our air force is in action." Now, the reality was that your air force was in action from time to time throughout the conflict, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, your air force could only be in action, apart from humanitarian matters and helicopters moving wounded around, could only be in action to bomb its own people.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. First of all, you can see that you're not well-versed in what an air force is. The effects of an air force depends on the type of planes. Fighter planes fight other planes. However, a helicopter transports. A transport plane transports. So when I say the air force, everything that flies is considered to be part of an air force. And when I said that our air force was operational, it meant that our helicopters could have flown, so that's the real answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Our air force is in action." This is on the 30th of April. It doesn't say "Our helicopters are flying," it says "Our air force is in action." It sounds as though it's in fighting mode.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Aircraft and helicopters together form aviation. Both make part of an aviation. And I'm telling you the information is centralised. The alerting is centralised. And I'm telling you it could have happened that planes or helicopters were flying somewhere in the north. All our units would be informed, would be alerted at the same time. It doesn't mean at all that the helicopter was flying in Kosovo and Metohija at the time. It don't necessarily mean that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go to the 16th of April, please. That we may not have a translation for. We don't have a translation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could you please place, Mr. Usher, page 22 of the original, marked "24 dan rata" or -- I think it's about right, and can you place that on the overhead projector. And for 1955 hours, entry number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see a reference, do we not, to reservists committing acts of rape and being taken into investigation followed by -- taken into custody and followed by investigation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, only they were not reservists. They were regular soldiers. They were my soldiers --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is it marked --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: -- they were not reservists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see in your diary, or your unit's diary, they were marked as reservists. We can see it in the second line. So how come they got marked as reservists if the truth is it was the regular soldiers who were accused of rape?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Because that was just the first information we got. And when we established their identity, I went there myself when it was established that they were regular soldiers. The information came from the MUP, and the original information also came from the MUP. The reservists and soldiers were dressed the same, and that's how the original confusion came about. You have documentation about that in the form of some criminal reports that were filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at the 21st of April, which is page 27, Mr. Usher. And at the foot of the page for this, at item number 7 -- further down, please. We still don't have translations, I think, for this. We see an entry right at the foot of the page -- right down, please. Push the page right up. That's it. I want to see the bottom of the page, please. Right. You've got to go -- we still can't see the bottom of the page. Can you push it so we can see the bottom entry on the page. The other way round, please, Mr. Usher. Can you push the page up so that I can see all of entry number 7. That's it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read entry number 7 to us, please, Mr. Djosan. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "21 member of the MUP was killed and seriously wounded in Meja village. The units were ordered to take measures of combat security and given tasks --" can't read this -- "information that there were 300 to 400 members of Siptar terrorist forces --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That will probably do for the present purposes. Before -- I'm going to come back to that entry, but just cast your eyes up the page, please. It's item number 2, so you'll have to move the document a little bit. Items 2 and 3. Can you just read out number 2, the 2.30 entry, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Action of enemy aviation against refugees from Maja villages."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness read into the microphone, please, and read again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Colonel. You're being asked by the interpreter to read into the microphone. Start again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Action of enemy aviation targeting the refugee settlement of Maja in the area of Bistrazin village. Airstrike effected with 32 projectiles of highly destructive power resulting in complete destruction of the settlement." That's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've read that as Meja in the area of Bistrazin village. Meja is in quotation marks, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Maja, Maja; not Meja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maja.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Maja was a name for that refugee settlement which housed refugees from Croatia, people who were expelled during the Storm and Flash Operations. There was a Serb refugees settlement, settlement of Serbs expelled from the territory of Serbia during the Croatian offensives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So here we find two things: First of all, we find at 2.30, when NATO bombs an area, you do record it, unlike that which happened at Nogavac, as you would say. And then at the foot of the page in the entry we first looked at, we see that there is a suggestion that a large number of MUP people had been killed at Meja. Two different words. Maja, M-a-j-a, Meja the village. So two points: First, do you record NATO bombing; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And secondly, before the operation against Meja starts at item 7 on this page, we see a recording of a large number of MUP people killed, is that right, in the Meja area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: To your first question, why there is this entry in the diary: Because the refugee settlement Maja is part of Djakovica. Secondly, we had our own unit in the area of Bistrazin that was guarding the Bistrazin bridge, and the airstrike could easily have been on the unit. And thirdly, Meja and Maja are completely different notions and completely different locations. The only thing they have in common are three letters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see a few days later, a few days after this entry in your war diary, under the operation that you explained was described as Reka operation, a large number of people died at Meja. Was this another example of killings being responsive by way of revenge?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you're asking me questions which are really not appropriate. I could easily ask you if the killing of that Brazilian man in London was responsive by way of revenge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Colonel, just please answer the question if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a general, but it's all the same. You can call me "Colonel" if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks for the correction, General.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next page, please. Next page, please. Mr. Djosan, you have been giving an account --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did we have an answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I've given him a chance to answer it. He's given the answer he's given. It's kind of negative. It's up to him how he answers these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would appreciate it if you would repeat the question and I will answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, there was no killing by way of revenge or retaliation. There was a combat against terrorists, and terrorists got killed in combat, just as my soldiers did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Except that my soldiers were more often killed in ambushes and because they stepped on mines or because they were kidnapped. But nobody was killed by way of retaliation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've given an account of NATO bombardment, and the picture you have painted may have been of almost continuous bombardment. Would you look, please, at the next page, which is -- yes, that's the page, and read out the first entry for the 22nd of April for us.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "In the last 24 hours, intensive flying over by enemy aviation in the area of defence of the brigade was like in the previous days. There was no airstrike on brigade units, nor did we attack them because they were moving outside the reach of successful targeting by our weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two pages further on, please. Again on the first entry. This is the -- two pages further on. 32nd -- Mr. Nort. Mr. Nort, that's the one. The 32nd day of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the first entry for this page, please, Mr. Djosan.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. "Action of enemy aviation in the zone of the brigade was absent. Over-flights were effected like on the previous day. Our units did not fire because the targets were outside our zone of activity, outside our range."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next page, please, Mr. Nort. The 33rd day of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read the first entry again for us, and now I think we have -- we have translations into English to be followed.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The intensity of enemy over-flights as yesterday. There were no airstrikes at the combat disposition of the units of the brigade. We did not fire at them because they flew outside the range of our weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the last entry on this topic -- would be on the next page, please, Mr. Nort, the 34th day of the war, and it's the entry at 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Shall I begin with the first entry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it's relevant to this topic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: It seems to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're quite right. "Four missiles were sent into the Devet Jugovica barracks." Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "In the earning morning hours enemy aviation intensively struck against installations in the zone of the brigade with four projectiles there fired at the Devet Jugovica barracks." That's in the centre of Djakovica, I want to add.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... but then if we go over to 1900 hours, we see again as a reflection of their level, or the strike rate of air attack --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Due to bad weather and rain, the intensity of activity by enemy aviation was lower." Of course, when the weather is bad, planes don't fly so often. However, they were able to fire, to effect airstrikes regardless of the rain, in view of the tactics they were applying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these last few entries that I've asked you to read out show that it was by no means daily attack on your area, or anything like it, was it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. There were daily airstrikes. I'm just telling you this diary was kept in Djakovica. That was the headquarters of the brigade, and there was one artillery battalion in Bec, which is slightly further away from Djakovica. So if there were airstrikes in Prizren, they were not striking installations of the brigade. Airstrikes were a daily occurrence. And when I say "daily occurrence," I mean by day and by night. It's just that they didn't hit one of our installations every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Chamber will recall, looking at the page displayed at the moment, that this is the first reference we found to the "Reka" operation. I needn't repeat that, but just to remind you, and if Mr. Nort would just display the next page and we can see in the English the 27th, now that we have it translated. There's the next reference we've been able to find to Reka at 0600 hours, where it says: "The action of --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd like to read out the entry at 0600 just again so we've got the precise words that you would use, or that were used in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I read this three or four days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just read that one sentence. "The action of --"

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The action of mopping up of Siptar terrorists forces, Reka, began in which the following forces are participating --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Ciscenje" is the word?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: 1 MB of the first light rocket -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Ciscenje" means -- it's been translated as "mopping up," but does it also mean "cleansing"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. "Ciscenje" means separating the good from the bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: If you take it as a word. That meant separating the terrorists from the rest of the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we've been told by the accused that the term "ethnic cleansing" was first applied in respect of sufferings by the Serbs. Is the word "Ciscenje" used for ethnic cleansing? Help us.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Ethnic cleansing" and "Ciscenje" are different things. Ethnic cleansing has now taken place in Kosovo and Metohija, and it is now ethnically really pure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm right, aren't I, that the phrase "ethnic cleansing" --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, you're not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd let me ask the question first, Mr. Djosan. The phrase "ethnic cleansing" in your language has, as one of its two words, the word "Ciscenje"; correct? Simple question.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You give your answer by your reply.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please don't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please give the answer. I didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't really answer, that's why you didn't hear me. Ethnic cleansing is a notion that was imposed and introduced to indicate that Serbs were doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me give you the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Serbs are completely absent from Kosovo. There are no Serbs in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question that was asked was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that's a real ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question that was asked was whether in your language the term "ethnic cleansing" has as one of its words "Ciscenje."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our language -- there are two words in our language for that and one of them is "Ciscenje." "Etnicko ciscenje" is a term that consists two of words, the last of them, the second of them being "Ciscenje."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we can go to the 28th of April, the Chamber will simply find again that -- putting its evidence and memory perhaps in context, a third reference to the Reka plan on the fifth line of the entry on the 28th of April, the 36th day of the war. I don't need to go through that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell us this, Mr. Djosan: Have you been thinking about your evidence? Has it occurred to you where we might be able to find a copy of the Reka plan?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: First of all, plan of the Operation Reka -- first of all, it was not an operation. It was an action, an anti-terrorist action. You should distinguish between those two terms. "Operation" is a much larger notion. It implies greater forces and a larger area and takes a longer time. Second, my unit did take part in that anti-terrorist action, and I gave you an explanation. The complete plan is something that I don't have. Every unit gets the relevant excerpt for its own action. My part of the task was to defend the axis towards Cabrat. I told you that a couple of days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have your evidence on that, and what you described it as was an assignment to prevent the grouping of Siptar terrorist forces rallying in their Carragojs valley.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Carragojs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that. And you knew that the plan - it was your terminology - the plan was called Reka. Well, I still ask you: Do you know where we can find a copy of this plan?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's something I don't know. I know about the orders I received for my unit. Each unit gets its own task, its own assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, if we look at Delic's diary for the same period, and I don't have time to with you, but if we look at Delic's diary for the same period, we will find no reference to the word "Reka." So here we have a plan of great importance and at the end of which a large number of people lay dead. Can you explain to us how such an important plan has a name - a code name - in your diary that doesn't appear as a code name in the diary or any other documentation of your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Which superior officer do you mean? Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Delic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Delic was not my commander. He was not my superior officer. We were colleges. He was the commander of one brigade, and I was commander of another brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, can you explain, then, how people involved in the same operation will not be using the same code term to describe it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: First of all, it was not an operation. It was an anti-terrorist action. In Kosovo and Metohija, a total of three anti-terrorist actions took place during the entire aggression. One was the anti-terrorist operation in 1998. Another operation was the aggressive operation of the air force, and the third was the defensive operation of the army of Yugoslavia. There were only three operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if Lazarevic is the superior to whom you're concerned, should we be able to find reference -- is your superior. Can you -- where shall we find reference in either his records or his archives to this Reka plan, so that we can know what was really planned? And I'm using the word "planned" because, in translation, that's what you described it as a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Did I say that it was called "Reka Operation" or did I say it was a plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... away from the argument about whether it's an operation or a plan or an action. You know what the questions are about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an anti-terrorist action, and it would be very wrong to say that the army of Yugoslavia undertook an operation against such small forces. An operation implies the use of forces the size of a corps or larger, and in this action a relatively small number of soldiers and policemen were involved. That cannot be an operation. An operation is defined by the forces, the time, and the area for which they fought. And if we now start saying that operations were being effected everywhere, then we would make it sound like the Second World War or something. And as to the second part of your question about the plan of General Lazarevic, how could I know about the plans of my superior officer, his documentation? Anyway, it's not his documentation. It's the documentation of the corps. Our superior officers do not have their own documentation. Just like Djosan's diary: It's not Djosan's diary, it's the diary of his brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question on this and then I'm going to move on because I want to finish as soon as I possibly can. If we look at Delic's diary for the same period, we'll find plans that are much broader in scope than the particular Reka plan that you were concerned with. Was there a larger plan of which Reka was an integral part; and if so, what was the name of the larger plan?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. My knowledge is reflected in the diary. Whatever I knew is in the diary. If I had been aware of any other plan, it would have been reflected in the diary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can do no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Chamber may be interested, or the accused may be interested in finding, there's another reference to rapes on the 2nd of May, I think, with investigation. I mention that for completeness. I'm not going to go into it in detail. If we can go, please, Mr. Nort, to page 41, the 44th day of the war, and to the entry at 1800. This is for -- and we -- we don't, I think, have this, unfortunately, translated, but if we look at 1800, please, Mr. Nort. Right down at the bottom of the page. We see here a reference to plan called -- or something called "Silo." Or Silo. Silo - I'm grateful - it's got a diacritic on top of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read out the sentence that ends in "Silo" so that we can see what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. First I'd like to say something in relation to what you said about rape. There were individual cases. Both were attempted rapes, and you do have the documentation about this. Every such individual case was prosecuted. So let's deal with that straight away. I don't want to omit referring to that kind of thing. As for Silo, what is written here, I don't know what you're specifically interested in. Are you interested in what silo is? That is a type of a rocket system for air defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's what it is. I'm not concerned. I'm trying to decipher your document and to see how it may assist Chamber. Let's move on, then, please, to page 47, the 49th date of war, 12th of May. Again on the -- it's the entry at 16 -- just above 1600, Mr. Nort, please. Here we see another reference at the end of this entry to something involving VP and then "Skore," which I think probably means Ceasar. Is this a code word? What does it mean, "Skore"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. First of all, I don't think it's "Skore." It's "Skoze." Yes, Skoze. It's an elevation where we place our rocket system in order to fire at the air force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We see, and you -- I can take you to the references, but will you accept that in the period of May you were sending to Pristina regularly for reinforcements? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were sending for reinforcements to Pristina. For example, on page 52, the 54th day of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Nort, page 52, 54th day of the war, and the entry at 1320.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here you are recording that you -- the brigade has sought reinforcements from Pristina; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And there are other entries to the like effect. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to know what kind of reinforcement and in what sense. There can be reinforcements in different ways. We asked for air defence reinforcements because the most intensive airstrikes by NATO were at that time in Metohija parallel to the aggressor strikes coming from Albania. That is to say the stronger the terrorist attacks from Albania were, the more there were NATO airstrikes in Metohija. That is why we sought reinforcement in the terms of PDO, the air defence systems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go to page 53, the 55th day of the war, in this 1610 entry we can see that you were actually getting whole fresh units from Pristina, weren't you? It wasn't just -- you were actually getting more units. And just think back, please. Why did you need more units?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you're asking me things that you don't know about. I cannot get any kind of equipment without soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General. General, answer the question. Leave aside the comments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we asked for reinforcements, that meant that we were asking for an air defence unit. You cannot get equipment without getting the manpower you need. In my unit, I had the exact number of people required for manning the equipment we had. An aircraft without a pilot doesn't mean a thing. The same goes for our units. When we asked for reinforcements, we asked for a unit of the air defence to come in. That is the manpower or the personnel that you're speaking of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm going to suggest to you that the whole purpose of getting reinforcements is because the plan to move the population was under way. Would you go now, please, to the 56th day of the war --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think he must answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I don't think you're right on that at all, and I think that your line of thinking is tendentious. How could I move the population out with air defence systems? I already told you that that could have happened only if they were on aircraft.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 56th day of the war, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood, but I thought your immediately preceding answer was to the effect that you can't work the systems without men and therefore you had to have men as part of the reinforcements. Was that not the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what Mr. Nice is suggesting is you didn't need the men for the air defence systems, you need the men to help with the movement of the population. So why don't you deal with that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that it is pointless to answer that kind of question. I have explained that air defence only operates against an aviation. So if we asked for anti-aircraft defence reinforcements, we were asking for them in order to be able to fire back. And you know that there were airstrikes every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are only three more pages that I want you to look at. 56th day of the war, then, please, the 18th of May. If we go down to the bottom of the page, at 16.30. This is the third time you get reinforcements, by my calculation, from Pristina. Perhaps you'd read that entry, just -- just the entry for 16.30.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. "The Chief of Staff goes for the third time in succession to Pristina in order to take over the reinforcement unit and to bring it into the brigade."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, then, we'll look at the next entry. The Chamber will --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Will you now then -- we'll look at the next entry. The Chamber will immediately recognise the second word on the next entry. Perhaps you would be good enough to read the entry out.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The action of cleaning up the terrain in the villages south-west of Cabrat, reported by AKM." That is the forward command post of the Pristina corps. Our two firing platoons were supposed to take part in it --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: -- from the logistics part and from the other part of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, our interpreters have used the word "mopping up" or "cleaning up" for "Ciscenje," and we know that it features in the phrase, or is one of the words that features in the phrase "ethnic cleansing." Here, in context, cleaning up the villages to the south-west of Cabrat, that was ethnic cleansing you were engaged in, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Of course that was not the case. It was not ethnic cleansing, it was cleansing from terrorists. And the word "cleansing" or "clean-up" means separating something from the other. When you're cleaning your apartment, for instance, I imagine you leave the apartment intact, you just get the rubbish out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Djosan, is this an example of men within your brigade being used for purposes other than air defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the unit from time to time, at different points in time, when necessary, on orders from the superior command, took part in that. That's the unit that was called the intervention unit, and it consisted of two platoons of -- and it consisted of soldiers whose speciality was infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that two platoons reinforced by units from Pristina on three occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. No. A platoon cannot receive reinforcements. Reinforcements from Pristina were received only in terms of anti-aircraft equipment as the airstrikes against our forces and the civilian population in towns was intensified. That is to say, bombing by NATO aviation. As soon as the NATO Air Force strikes stopped, these reinforcements were no longer needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 57th day of the war, please, 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The 18.50 entry, please, Mr. Nort. Thank you very much. Immediately on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd like to read for us the 18.50 entry.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "From the IKM of the Pristina Corps we received orders that this delayed action of cleansing or cleaning up villages below Cabrat should be realised on the 20th of May and that the planned units should be at their position for departure at 5.00 in the morning."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the cleaning up, what you would say the separation, I think, of the terrorists from the good people is planned in advance with units, and it's got a start time at 5.00 the following morning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you go to the following day, the 58th day of the war --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Let me just finish, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had our units in that area, and there were a great many terrorists there. It was necessary to provide security for our units against the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But these units that are being delayed -- put on a delayed start until 5.00 the following morning are going to do the cleaning up, cleansing, mopping up, separation, whatever it is described by the word "Ciscenje," yes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. My unit or, rather, part of my unit; two platoons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's go over, then, to page -- the 58th day of the war. The 20th of May. The 5.00 entry at the top, which is what we would expect. Read that out for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Units for clearing up from our unit --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please read slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, the interpreter is asking you to read more slowly and into the microphone. Would you just read that again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Units for clean-up from our composition, that is to say one platoon from the logistics and one platoon from the command at the ordered time should take the departing positions as they are ready to carry out the set assignment."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the clean-up units being sent off to Cabrat, I think, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we go to 17.50 on the same page. And if there's anything significant in the middle, you must let me know about it, but if we go to 17.50 on the same page, read that entry out, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Units that took part in clearing the terrain returned to their original units. The task was carried out successfully without any losses."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell us, please, separating out the KLA from the others, how many people died, how many people taken prisoner, where is it all recorded?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: My units were only in the blockade. My units did not have contact with the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Units are sent off at 5.00, as we can see, to do whatever is meant by "Ciscenje." The operation is successful --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and there have been no losses on your side. Can we find out, please, what actually happened. Were people killed? Were people arrested? Were people moved out? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Units that took part in clearing up the terrain returned to their original units. The task was successfully carried out without any losses." That is to say the task that the unit had was carried out. That means that they were on the blockade line and that they did not have any losses and that they were not engaged in any operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Djosan, we are trying to work out through the contemporaneous documents that come late to hand what happened, and I must suggest to you that this diary of yours shows that you were actually engaged in the processes of ethnic cleansing. And the reason it doesn't find reflection in, for example, Delic's diary, these entries of yours, is because what you were doing was wrong and you all knew it.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's not correct. My units are only -- or, rather, only a small part of my units that were in Djakovica were engaged from time to time in protecting primarily their own combat order; their own combat order. And every unit has the right and duty to protect the order and deployment of its own units. That is not ethnic cleansing. That was only fighting against terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm grateful for the time to deal with that document. Its production as an exhibit, it may or may not be that the Chamber would prefer to put all parts of this diary together comprehensively or it may want to exhibit them separately. The translations are, of course, draft translations and I'm sorry that we weren't able to guess in advance which other pages we would -- our research has subsequently shown would find of value to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nice. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, would it have been possible to use some word other than "Ciscenje" in relation to the action you were taking against the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think that the word "Ciscenje" in a way was a clumsy choice, but it was used very often. Whoever kept the diary, the operations officer, often used it -- or, rather, this word was often used irrespective of what was actually being done. Specifically, the word itself, "Ciscenje," really has a very broad meaning, but it was customary. It was used often, and sometimes quite simply it was used in order to record things faster, to write them down faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you just tell us again what -- what you say it means in the context in which we saw it referred to perhaps five or six times.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: It was used -- in the concrete context, it means that this was fighting against terrorists, Siptar terrorists, in certain places where an action was being carried out. So that means that this was only fighting against terrorists who were fighting against our units, who were resisting them, et cetera. This does not mean at all that the population were the targets of the military and the police. After all, there was a witness here from Osek Hilja, from Cabrat, from that area who talked about this. My unit was in Osek Hilja all the time and there weren't any problems at all. But there were places where our units sustained major losses, especially as the aggression continued, there were more and more terrorists in urban areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It was only used in relation to the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Terrorists only, yes. When it says "Ciscenje," it meant removing them, taking them captive, and even killing terrorists in a war. That is to say, destroying terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: If they could be taken prisoner, of course they were taken prisoner, but fighting went on. But it was terrorists only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, is there anything arising from this phase of the cross-examination that you might wish to take up in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just a few questions. Further re-examination by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, Mr. Nice quoted page 6 to you, trying to prove that it was contradictory to your statement, that every day there were bombing campaigns during the aggression. Was the bombing campaign a daily occurrence in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 6, it says: "Airstrikes of NATO. There weren't any NATO airstrikes at the positions of our brigade."

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that there were no airstrikes relates only to the positions of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The positions of my unit only. And the buildings or, rather, the positions where my units are, Cabrat, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's not waste time. On the top of that page, it says at 8.45 the air alert signal went off. What does this say here? ODH what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The observation station from the Metervojnovic [phoen] barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then it says that NATO struck several times, the NATO Air Force.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this day that he chose out of context, he claims that there was no activity because there weren't any airstrikes against your unit.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: There was activity every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a single day in Kosovo when there were no NATO activities?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I do not recall a single day in Kosovo and Metohija without any NATO activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning, Mr. Nice asked you about Nogavac, and you responded that at first our air force was flying. Our air force, was it flying over Kosovo and Metohija during the aggression?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that it was flying, you are referring to other parts of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in Kosovo they had to respect air supremacy; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's, of course, a leading question which takes no account of the text, and it shouldn't have been asked by the accused, as he knows, because when he says, When you're referring, you're referring to other parts of Yugoslavia, the text needs to be examined to see what it says. It doesn't say that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you are to avoid leading questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this question was not a leading question at all. It was just a yes/no question, and he gave his answer. So it was not a leading question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nice showed you page 22 here and said that a group of reservists was referred to here. What does it say here at 19.55 on page 22? Could I please read it out, or could you read it out?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can. At 19.55: "We were informed by the MUP that a group of reservists in the village of Crmljanje are carrying out rapes and robbery. The commander ordered that --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please read slower. The interpreters cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General. General, you're being asked by the interpreters to read more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you don't have to read the first part that you quoted when Mr. Nice said so, but in this first part, does it say, "We were informed by the MUP"? This -- is this the information that you recorded the MUP informed you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now please read out the part that Mr. Nice didn't want you to read, that is to say the commander ordered, what Mr. Nice didn't ask you.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The commander ordered -" that is to say I ordered - "that the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the PVO, who was stationed there, together with the head of the security organ and the Military Police Platoon, carry out an on-site investigation and arrest the perpetrators." So these were not reservists, they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You established that after the investigation, but you recorded here what the MUP informed you, what you ordered. You ordered for people to go out and arrest the perpetrators. Thank you, General. Let us just have a look at this, this page that has to do with the relevant date, the 27th. That is page 33. This was often mentioned here. A few days ago you quoted this and now as well. So what does this say here? "The action of cleaning up the STS, the Siptar terrorist forces." Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The action of cleaning up the Siptar terrorist forces has started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General. So "Ciscenje" in relation to Siptar terrorist forces, can it pertain to anything else but to what it does pertain to, that is to say the Siptar terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That only; nothing else. That is to say, neutralising the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of any measures of that kind being taken against the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was anything done to help the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, you just used the word "neutralising," for "Ciscenje." That's the first time I've heard that. Can it have that meaning as well, to neutralise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've told you a few moments ago that the word "Ciscenje" in a way became customary and sometimes for practical reasons it was used. Maybe it should have said all the time "the Ciscenje of Siptar terrorist forces," but "neutralising" could also be an adequate and appropriate word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 28, which also pertains to this action Reka. It says: "Brief discussion among the command organs of the brigade where it was pointed out --" what was pointed out here? At 0700 hours. You have a meeting of your commanders.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't have that page here with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 34. A few moments ago Mr. Nice showed you that page. That is the 28th. That's the date.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The -- page 34, the 36th day of the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "Short meeting of the organs of the brigade command on the daily engagement, where it was stressed --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then colon.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Then colon. "Intervention unit would be engaged in Reka." No. It says, "Intervention unit continues to be engaged in the Reka action."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else was pointed out here? "Intervention unit continues to be engaged in the Reka action."

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The chief of engineering and the chief of ABHO, if the Terzanski and Ivanski bridge were to be destroyed, alternative routes should be used, that there should be relocation of the command post."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this is your morning meeting.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is stated here is that, inter alia, what was discussed at that meeting, that the intervention unit is still engaged in that action, continues to be engaged.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said action is evolving according to plan and the dynamics involved, does that mean that you have to have a written plan for this action Reka, or is this the written plan for the Reka operation? Is it customary, since you're a professional soldier, to have a written plan for this kind of action or is this part of a general anti-terrorist effort? Have you heard of a written plan for Reka?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I did not see this plan, but I heard of it. I heard of the Reka plan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your unit had assignments there on both days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it held a blockade line for both days.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, at Cabrat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have any contact with the terrorist groups, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't go into operation, into action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, we didn't go into action. We didn't use any ammunition. We didn't have any casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. On the 30th of April here, Mr. Nice - and that's page 36 - quoted your entry here in the diary: "Signal sounded means the end of danger from the air SCVK." What does that all mean? "The operative centre was ordered not to open target -- open fire on targets in the air because our air force is in action. OCPRK ordered not to ..." et cetera. Now, tell me, our air force, did our air force carry out any assignment of the bombing of any target in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any such assignment, and I would have to have known if it had existed. And as has been reported here that our air force would be flying, I would have to know with certainty of each specific case and concrete case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Let me just take a moment to find my way in these notes and entries. Ah, yes. Now, Mr. Nice placed page 27 before you. The 21st of April is the date, and it was linked to -- well, actually he made some confusion between Meja and Maja and you explained that to us, but read out what it says -- read out what it says -- it was the 29th day of the war, the 27th page, at 0230 hours. The actions of enemy planes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The action of enemy air force at the refugee camp of Maja in the area of Bistrazin village, and this attack used 23 projectiles of great destructive power, and as a result the whole settlement was completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. He asked you to start reading that passage and then you didn't go further. What does it say further on? What's the next entry?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "A team from the brigade toured the region where the action had taken place, the action by enemy air force -" that is to say in brackets the Maja refugee camp - "and came across an atrocious site. Six persons killed, 32 were wounded, of which 18 seriously wounded and one child was in a critical state. The material damage was complete."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you provided us with an explanation as to why this kind of attack was entered, an entry was made of it. Did part of your unit go on the spot, on site?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was in my area. It was near the bridge at Bistrazin, where we had a unit of ours stationed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what does it say in 20? One member, a MUP member was killed and one seriously wounded in the village of Meja; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to that, we have the next entry, and tell us what that says. What does your next entry say?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: It says one member of the MUP was killed, one was seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next sentence? What's the next sentence? Read it out.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The units were ordered to take measures of combat -- providing combat security and carry out tasks to --" just a minute, let me decipher this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says west, something west of; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: "The units were ordered to take measures of combat security and -- west of Cabrat, and the information that west of Cabrat there were 300 to 400 terrorist forces or, rather, Siptars --" in brackets it says "members of the Siptars, STC -- STS." So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 20 and 2000 -- 2400 hours, you were asked to raise your security readiness, combat security readiness; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So combat security readiness, does that mean an attack or what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, it means to step up our awareness and alertness and our guards and everything, and to prepare for a possible attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So you received information at the same time you were asked to raise your readiness, alert readiness, that there were 400 Siptar terrorists, about 400, 3 to 400. Now, how many of your men were in the area, those that manned the air defence weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: In Cabrat there were about a hundred of my soldiers of my unit -- members of my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: They provided security for the command post of the brigade and catered to that command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, naturally I'd like to complete this witness's testimony before taking the break, but if you are going to be very much longer, then we will have to take the break. How much longer will you be?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't need too much -- too much longer, but another ten minutes, I think, because quite obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand one hour and 45 minutes is the limit. We'll take the break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Djosan, Mr. Nice showed you the 28th page, where it says: "In the last 24 hours -" if you can take a look - "there were intensive flights by enemy air force in the zone." And he showed you several examples of your entries where you record on page 30, for example, using almost the same words, that there were intensive flights but that the targets were outside the area which could be reached and targeted and out of range of your weapons. So he mentioned some of these entries of yours made in your diary. What does this point to? Can you see the intensity of the action or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: What we can see here is the intensity of the action by the fact that we did not respond to the planes flying overhead outside the range of our own equipment. In view of the range of our equipment, we were not able to target those planes for which we were certain we wouldn't be able to down them. And they were flying at extremely high altitudes, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your entries just relate to the positions of your brigade and nothing else and how that was affected -- and they were affected; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nice showed you page 38, where at 1600 hours, what does it say there? From MUP information received. What does it say? Read it out, please, yourself. He said that there was some rapes mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Information received from MUP told us that a group of soldiers had carried out rapes in Osek Hilja. The commander ordered a detailed investigation and urgent steps to be taken -- energetic steps to be taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened, actually?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: There was a rape attempt on the part of one soldier in Osek Hilja, and we received information from MUP to that effect. We sent a security organ there to check the situation out, and a military police unit, and handed that soldier over to the court-martial in Pristina, along with a criminal report against him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. One more question. You explained to us or, rather, to Mr. Nice a moment ago what kind of reinforcements you sought. Can you be more precise and tell us what reinforcements you actually received, if you remember. If not, you needn't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. First of all, we received a Tuba [phoen] battery of rocket systems when Cimbaljevic and Ivanovic, two of my soldiers, were killed. They were in Metohija for two days and returned. After that, the PUB type. Then we received several Bofors type cannons and a modified RR4 weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, please: These reinforcements, the ones you received, were they exclusively for anti-air action or air defence action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, they were exclusively air defence weapons, the -- for targeting targets in the air at higher altitudes and with higher range. But the Bofors type of cannon was exclusively designed for anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, guns and cannons have their crews and so does this PUB system; is that right? Now, did a single soldier from that crew that you received as reinforcements take part in any other activities except for the anti-aircraft defence systems?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DJOSAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, never. They were exclusively reinforcements, and their officers were there. Their commanding officers were there to command them. They were sent with them and they were included into my unit, but those soldiers were commanded over by the commanding officers of those units, and they were not deployed for any other purpose except anti-aircraft action, that is to say to target enemy planes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more point, Mr. Robinson, if I may. I received from the liaison officer a copy of this document here. It is from Mr. Nice's office, from the OTP, and the title of it is - I had it in the Serbian language - "Final report to the Prosecutor by the committee established to review the NATO bombing campaign against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." That's the title.
